verses.decoded: And Adoraim, and Lachish, and Azekah,

verses.kjv: And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin fenced cities.
verses.decoded: And Zorah, and Aijalon, and Hebron, which are fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.

verses.kjv: And he fortified the strong holds, and put captains in them, and store of victual, and of oil and wine.
verses.decoded: He strengthened the fortresses, placed commanders in them, and stored supplies of food, oil, and wine.

verses.kjv: And in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.
verses.decoded: And in each city he placed shields and spears, and made them very strong, with Judah and Benjamin supporting him.

verses.kjv: And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts.
verses.decoded: The priests and the Levites throughout all Israel came to him from all their regions.

verses.kjv: For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord:
verses.decoded: The Levites left their homes and property and went to Judah and Jerusalem because Jeroboam and his sons had stopped them from serving as priests for the LORD.

verses.kjv: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.
verses.decoded: He appointed priests for the high places, for the idols, and for the calves that he had made.

verses.kjv: And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.decoded: After them, from all the tribes of Israel, those who decided to seek the LORD God of Israel came to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the LORD God of their ancestors.

verses.kjv: So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.
verses.decoded: So they made the kingdom of Judah stronger and made Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, powerful for three years, because for three years they followed the ways of David and Solomon.

verses.kjv: And Rehoboam took him Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David to wife, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse;
verses.decoded: And Rehoboam married Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth, who was the son of David, and Abihail, the daughter of Eliab, who was the son of Jesse;

verses.kjv: Which bare him children; Jeush, and Shamariah, and Zaham.
verses.decoded: She gave birth to his children: Jeush, Shamariah, and Zaham.

verses.kjv: And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; which bare him Abijah, and Attai, and Ziza, and Shelomith.
verses.decoded: After her, he married Maachah, the daughter of Absalom; she gave birth to Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

verses.kjv: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and begat twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.)
verses.decoded: And Rehoboam loved Maachah, the daughter of Absalom, more than all his other wives and concubines. (For he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.)

verses.kjv: And Rehoboam made Abijah the son of Maachah the chief, to be ruler among his brethren: for he thought to make him king.
verses.decoded: And Rehoboam appointed Abijah, the son of Maachah, as the leader over his brothers because he intended to make him king.

verses.kjv: And he dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin, unto every fenced city: and he gave them victual in abundance. And he desired many wives.
verses.decoded: He acted wisely and sent all his children throughout all the regions of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city, and he provided them with plenty of food. He also wanted many wives.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
verses.decoded: After Rehoboam had established the kingdom and made himself strong, he abandoned the law of the LORD, and all Israel followed him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord,
verses.decoded: It happened that in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem because they had disobeyed the LORD.

verses.kjv: With twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen: and the people were without number that came with him out of Egypt; the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
verses.decoded: With twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and countless people who came with him from Egypt; the Lubim, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.

verses.kjv: And he took the fenced cities which pertained to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: He captured the fortified cities that belonged to Judah and then went to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
verses.decoded: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the leaders of Judah, who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "This is what the LORD says: You have abandoned me, so I have also handed you over to Shishak."

verses.kjv: Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The Lord is righteous.
verses.decoded: Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, The LORD is just.

verses.kjv: And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
verses.decoded: When the LORD saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; so I will not destroy them, but I will give them some relief; and my anger will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.
verses.decoded: However, they will be his servants so that they may learn about my service and the service of the kingdoms of other nations.

verses.kjv: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
verses.decoded: Then Shishak, king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem and took away the treasures from the temple of the LORD and the treasures from the king’s palace; he took everything. He also took the gold shields that Solomon had made.

verses.kjv: Instead of which king Rehoboam made shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the chief of the guard, that kept the entrance of the king’s house.
verses.decoded: King Rehoboam made bronze shields and gave them to the commander of the royal guard, who was in charge of guarding the entrance to the king’s palace.

verses.kjv: And when the king entered into the house of the Lord, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.
verses.decoded: When the king entered the house of the LORD, the guards came and took them and brought them back into the guardroom.

verses.kjv: And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the Lord turned from him, that he would not destroy him altogether: and also in Judah things went well.
verses.decoded: When he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him so that He did not completely destroy him; and things also went well in Judah.

verses.kjv: So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem, and reigned: for Rehoboam was one and forty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother’s name was Naamah an Ammonitess.
verses.decoded: So King Rehoboam made himself strong in Jerusalem and ruled. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to rule, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother’s name was Naamah, an Ammonite woman.

verses.kjv: And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the Lord.
verses.decoded: He did evil because he did not make up his mind to seek the LORD.

verses.kjv: Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
verses.decoded: The events of Rehoboam's reign, from beginning to end, are recorded in the book of Shemaiah the prophet and in the records of Iddo the seer about family histories. There were constant wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

verses.kjv: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abijah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.decoded: Rehoboam died and was buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah became king in his place.

verses.kjv: Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam began Abijah to reign over Judah.
verses.decoded: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam's reign, Abijah began to rule over Judah.

verses.kjv: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.decoded: He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was also Michaiah, the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. There was a war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

verses.kjv: And Abijah set the battle in array with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men: Jeroboam also set the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, being mighty men of valour.
verses.decoded: Abijah arranged his army for battle with 400,000 brave and chosen warriors. Jeroboam also arranged his army against him with 800,000 chosen men who were mighty and courageous.

verses.kjv: And Abijah stood up upon mount Zemaraim, which is in mount Ephraim, and said, Hear me, thou Jeroboam, and all Israel;
verses.decoded: And Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, which is in Mount Ephraim, and said, Listen to me, Jeroboam, and all Israel;

verses.kjv: Ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
verses.decoded: Shouldn't you know that the LORD God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a permanent covenant?

verses.kjv: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, is risen up, and hath rebelled against his lord.
verses.decoded: But Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who was a servant of Solomon, the son of David, has risen up and rebelled against his master.

verses.kjv: And there are gathered unto him vain men, the children of Belial, and have strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tenderhearted, and could not withstand them.
verses.decoded: And worthless men, the children of wickedness, gathered to him and made themselves strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon, because Rehoboam was young and sensitive, and could not resist them.

verses.kjv: And now ye think to withstand the kingdom of the Lord in the hand of the sons of David; and ye be a great multitude, and there are with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.
verses.decoded: And now you think you can oppose the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of the sons of David; and you are a large group, and you have golden calves with you, which Jeroboam made for you as gods.

verses.kjv: Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of them that are no gods.
verses.decoded: Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made yourselves priests like the nations of other countries? So that anyone who comes to dedicate himself with a young bull and seven rams can be a priest for those who are not gods.

verses.kjv: But as for us, the Lord is our God, and we have not forsaken him; and the priests, which minister unto the Lord, are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites wait upon their business:
verses.decoded: But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned him; the priests who serve the LORD are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites attend to their duties.

verses.kjv: And they burn unto the Lord every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense: the shewbread also set they in order upon the pure table; and the candlestick of gold with the lamps thereof, to burn every evening: for we keep the charge of the Lord our God; but ye have forsaken him.
verses.decoded: And they burned burnt offerings and sweet incense to the LORD every morning and every evening; they also arranged the showbread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps to burn every evening, because we obey the commands of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned him.

verses.kjv: And, behold, God himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Israel, fight ye not against the Lord God of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper.
verses.decoded: Look, God himself is with us as our leader, and his priests are blowing trumpets to warn you. O children of Israel, do not fight against the LORD God of your ancestors, because you will not succeed.

verses.kjv: But Jeroboam caused an ambushment to come about behind them: so they were before Judah, and the ambushment was behind them.
verses.decoded: But Jeroboam arranged an ambush behind them: so they were in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them.

verses.kjv: And when Judah looked back, behold, the battle was before and behind: and they cried unto the Lord, and the priests sounded with the trumpets.
verses.decoded: When Judah looked back, they saw that the battle was in front of them and behind them. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.

verses.kjv: Then the men of Judah gave a shout: and as the men of Judah shouted, it came to pass, that God smote Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
verses.decoded: Then the men of Judah shouted, and as they shouted, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel in front of Abijah and Judah.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel fled before Judah: and God delivered them into their hand.
verses.decoded: The people of Israel ran away from Judah, and God allowed Judah to defeat them.

verses.kjv: And Abijah and his people slew them with a great slaughter: so there fell down slain of Israel five hundred thousand chosen men.
verses.decoded: Abijah and his people killed them with a great slaughter: so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel were killed.

verses.kjv: Thus the children of Israel were brought under at that time, and the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied upon the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.decoded: So the people of Israel were defeated at that time, and the people of Judah won because they trusted in the LORD God of their ancestors.

verses.kjv: And Abijah pursued after Jeroboam, and took cities from him, Beth-el with the towns thereof, and Jeshanah with the towns thereof, and Ephrain with the towns thereof.
verses.decoded: And Abijah chased after Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel and its surrounding towns, Jeshanah and its surrounding towns, and Ephrain and its surrounding towns.

verses.kjv: Neither did Jeroboam recover strength again in the days of Abijah: and the Lord struck him, and he died.
verses.decoded: Jeroboam did not regain his strength during the time Abijah was king; the LORD struck him, and he died.

verses.kjv: But Abijah waxed mighty, and married fourteen wives, and begat twenty and two sons, and sixteen daughters.
verses.decoded: But Abijah became powerful, married fourteen wives, and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

verses.kjv: And the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and his sayings, are written in the story of the prophet Iddo.
verses.decoded: The other events of Abijah's reign, his behavior, and his words are recorded in the account written by the prophet Iddo.

verses.kjv: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In his days the land was quiet ten years.
verses.decoded: Abijah died and was buried in the city of David, and his son Asa became king in his place. During Asa's reign, the land was peaceful for ten years.

verses.kjv: And Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God:
verses.decoded: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

verses.kjv: For he took away the altars of the strange gods, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves:
verses.decoded: Because he removed the altars of the foreign gods, the high places, destroyed the idols, and cut down the sacred trees.

verses.kjv: And commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.
verses.decoded: He commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their ancestors and to obey the law and the commandments.

verses.kjv: Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images: and the kingdom was quiet before him.
verses.decoded: He also removed the high places and the idols from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was peaceful under his rule.

verses.kjv: And he built fenced cities in Judah: for the land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because the Lord had given him rest.
verses.decoded: He built walled cities in Judah because the land was peaceful, and he did not have any wars during those years, since the LORD had given him peace.

verses.kjv: Therefore he said unto Judah, Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us; because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered.
verses.decoded: Therefore he said to Judah, Let us build these cities and surround them with walls, towers, gates, and bars while the land is still before us; because we have sought the LORD our God, we have sought him, and he has given us peace on every side. So they built and prospered.

verses.kjv: And Asa had an army of men that bare targets and spears, out of Judah three hundred thousand; and out of Benjamin, that bare shields and drew bows, two hundred and fourscore thousand: all these were mighty men of valour.
verses.decoded: Asa had an army of men who carried shields and spears, three hundred thousand from Judah; and from Benjamin, who carried shields and used bows, two hundred and eighty thousand: all of these were brave and strong warriors.

verses.kjv: And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came unto Mareshah.
verses.decoded: And Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of one million soldiers and three hundred chariots; and he came to Mareshah.

verses.kjv: Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
verses.decoded: Then Asa went out to fight against him, and they arranged their battle formation in the valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

verses.kjv: And Asa cried unto the Lord his God, and said, Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Lord, thou art our God; let not man prevail against thee.
verses.decoded: And Asa cried out to the LORD his God and said, LORD, it is nothing for you to help, whether with many or with those who have no power: help us, O LORD our God; for we trust in you, and in your name we go against this multitude. O LORD, you are our God; do not let man succeed against you.

verses.kjv: So the Lord smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.
verses.decoded: So the LORD struck down the Ethiopians in front of Asa and the people of Judah; and the Ethiopians ran away.

verses.kjv: And Asa and the people that were with him pursued them unto Gerar: and the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before the Lord, and before his host; and they carried away very much spoil.
verses.decoded: Asa and the people with him chased them all the way to Gerar, and the Ethiopians were defeated so badly that they could not recover. They were destroyed in the presence of the LORD and his army, and Asa and his people took a large amount of plunder.

verses.kjv: And they smote all the cities round about Gerar; for the fear of the Lord came upon them: and they spoiled all the cities; for there was exceeding much spoil in them.
verses.decoded: They attacked and defeated all the cities around Gerar because they were terrified by the LORD. They took everything from all the cities because there was a great amount of loot in them.

verses.kjv: They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: They also attacked the livestock tents, took many sheep and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded:
verses.decoded: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah, the son of Oded.

verses.kjv: And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear ye me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.
verses.decoded: And he went out to meet Asa and said to him, Listen to me, Asa, and all of Judah and Benjamin; The LORD is with you as long as you are with him; if you seek him, you will find him; but if you abandon him, he will abandon you.

verses.kjv: Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
verses.decoded: For a long time, Israel has been without the true God, without a priest to teach, and without the law.

verses.kjv: But when they in their trouble did turn unto the Lord God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.
verses.decoded: But when they were in trouble, they turned to the LORD God of Israel and sought him, and he was found by them.

verses.kjv: And in those times there was no peace to him that went out, nor to him that came in, but great vexations were upon all the inhabitants of the countries.
verses.decoded: At that time, there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in, but great troubles were on all the people living in the lands.

verses.kjv: And nation was destroyed of nation, and city of city: for God did vex them with all adversity.
verses.decoded: One nation was destroyed by another nation, and one city by another city, because God troubled them with every kind of trouble.

verses.kjv: Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.
verses.decoded: Be strong, and do not let your hands be weak, because your work will be rewarded.

verses.kjv: And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim, and renewed the altar of the Lord, that was before the porch of the Lord.
verses.decoded: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he became encouraged, removed the detestable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities he had taken from Mount Ephraim, and restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the LORD's porch.

verses.kjv: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
verses.decoded: He gathered all the people of Judah and Benjamin, along with the foreigners living among them from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, because many from Israel joined him when they realized that the LORD his God was with him.

verses.kjv: So they gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.decoded: So they gathered together in Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.

verses.kjv: And they offered unto the Lord the same time, of the spoil which they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
verses.decoded: At that time, they offered to the LORD from the plunder they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.

verses.kjv: And they entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
verses.decoded: They made an agreement to seek the LORD God of their ancestors with all their heart and with all their soul;

verses.kjv: That whosoever would not seek the Lord God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
verses.decoded: That anyone who would not seek the LORD God of Israel should be put to death, whether they are young or old, whether male or female.

verses.kjv: And they sware unto the Lord with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets.
verses.decoded: And they made a solemn promise to the LORD with a loud voice, shouting, and with trumpets and horns.

verses.kjv: And all Judah rejoiced at the oath: for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and the Lord gave them rest round about.
verses.decoded: All of Judah was happy about the promise because they had sworn it with all their heart and searched for God with all their desire; they found Him, and the LORD gave them peace all around.

verses.kjv: And also concerning Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa cut down her idol, and stamped it, and burnt it at the brook Kidron.
verses.decoded: Also, regarding Maachah, the mother of King Asa, he removed her from her position as queen because she had made an idol in a grove. Asa cut down her idol, crushed it, and burned it at the Kidron brook.

verses.kjv: But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
verses.decoded: But the high places were not removed from Israel; however, Asa's heart was fully committed throughout his life.

verses.kjv: And he brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.
verses.decoded: He brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated: silver, gold, and vessels.

verses.kjv: And there was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.decoded: And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

verses.kjv: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.decoded: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha, king of Israel, attacked Judah and built Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering Asa, king of Judah.

verses.kjv: Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,
verses.decoded: Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasures of the house of the LORD and from the king’s house, and sent it to Ben-hadad, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,

verses.kjv: There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
verses.decoded: There is an agreement between me and you, just as there was between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold; go and end your agreement with Baasha, king of Israel, so that he will leave me alone.

verses.kjv: And Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
verses.decoded: Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel; they attacked Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the supply cities of Naphtali.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.
verses.decoded: When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and stopped his work.

verses.kjv: Then Asa the king took all Judah; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah.
verses.decoded: Then King Asa gathered all of Judah; and they took away the stones of Ramah and the wood from it, which Baasha was using to build; and Asa used them to build Geba and Mizpah.

verses.kjv: And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the Lord thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.
verses.decoded: At that time Hanani the prophet came to Asa, king of Judah, and said to him, Because you have trusted in the king of Syria and have not trusted in the LORD your God, the army of the king of Syria has escaped from your control.

verses.kjv: Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because thou didst rely on the Lord, he delivered them into thine hand.
verses.decoded: Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a large army, with many chariots and horsemen? Yet, because you relied on the LORD, he gave them into your hand.

verses.kjv: For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
verses.decoded: The eyes of the LORD search all over the earth to show his strength on behalf of those whose hearts are fully committed to him. In this, you have acted foolishly; therefore, from now on you will have wars.

verses.kjv: Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. And Asa oppressed some of the people the same time.
verses.decoded: Then Asa became angry with the prophet and put him in prison because he was furious with him over this matter. At the same time, Asa also oppressed some of the people.

verses.kjv: And, behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.decoded: Look, the actions of Asa, from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.kjv: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.
verses.decoded: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became sick in his feet, and his illness became very severe. However, during his illness, he did not seek the Lord, but instead sought help from the doctors.

verses.kjv: And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.
verses.decoded: Asa died and was buried with his ancestors in the forty-first year of his reign.

verses.kjv: And they buried him in his own sepulchres, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odours and divers kinds of spices prepared by the apothecaries’ art: and they made a very great burning for him.
verses.decoded: They buried him in his own tombs, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and placed him on a bed filled with sweet smells and various kinds of spices prepared by the skill of the apothecaries; and they made a very large fire for him.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead, and strengthened himself against Israel.
verses.decoded: And Jehoshaphat, his son, became king in his place, and made himself strong against Israel.

verses.kjv: And he placed forces in all the fenced cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had taken.
verses.decoded: He stationed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and put military units in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father had captured.

verses.kjv: And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim;
verses.decoded: The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he followed the early practices of his father David and did not seek the Baals.

verses.kjv: But sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel.
verses.decoded: But he sought the LORD God of his father, and obeyed his commandments, and did not follow the practices of Israel.

verses.kjv: Therefore the Lord stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honour in abundance.
verses.decoded: Therefore the LORD established the kingdom in his control; and all of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat; and he had great wealth and honor.

verses.kjv: And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord: moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah.
verses.decoded: He was deeply committed to following the ways of the LORD; furthermore, he removed the high places and sacred groves from Judah.

verses.kjv: Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, even to Ben-hail, and to Obadiah, and to Zechariah, and to Nethaneel, and to Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.decoded: Also, in the third year of his reign, he sent to his leaders—Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethaneel, and Michaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah.

verses.kjv: And with them he sent Levites, even Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, priests.
verses.decoded: And with them he sent Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, who were Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, who were priests.

verses.kjv: And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.
verses.decoded: They taught in Judah, carrying the book of the law of the LORD with them, and traveled through all the cities of Judah, teaching the people.

verses.kjv: And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.
verses.decoded: The fear of the LORD came upon all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, so they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

verses.kjv: Also some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat presents, and tribute silver; and the Arabians brought him flocks, seven thousand and seven hundred rams, and seven thousand and seven hundred he goats.
verses.decoded: Also some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and tribute silver; and the Arabians brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly; and he built in Judah castles, and cities of store.
verses.decoded: And Jehoshaphat became very powerful; and he built fortresses and storage cities in Judah.

verses.kjv: And he had much business in the cities of Judah: and the men of war, mighty men of valour, were in Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: He had many responsibilities in the cities of Judah, and the soldiers, strong and brave warriors, were in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And these are the numbers of them according to the house of their fathers: Of Judah, the captains of thousands; Adnah the chief, and with him mighty men of valour three hundred thousand.
verses.decoded: These are their numbers according to their family groups: From Judah, the commanders of thousands; Adnah was the leader, and with him were three hundred thousand brave warriors.

verses.kjv: And next to him was Jehohanan the captain, and with him two hundred and fourscore thousand.
verses.decoded: Next to him was Jehohanan the captain, and with him were two hundred and eighty thousand.

verses.kjv: And next him was Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord; and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valour.
verses.decoded: Next to him was Amasiah, the son of Zichri, who willingly dedicated himself to the LORD; and with him were two hundred thousand strong and brave men.

verses.kjv: And of Benjamin; Eliada a mighty man of valour, and with him armed men with bow and shield two hundred thousand.
verses.decoded: And from Benjamin; Eliada was a mighty man of courage, and with him were two hundred thousand armed men with bow and shield.

verses.kjv: And next him was Jehozabad, and with him an hundred and fourscore thousand ready prepared for the war.
verses.decoded: Next to him was Jehozabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand soldiers fully prepared for war.

verses.kjv: These waited on the king, beside those whom the king put in the fenced cities throughout all Judah.
verses.decoded: These served the king, along with those whom the king placed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

verses.kjv: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab.
verses.decoded: Now Jehoshaphat had great wealth and honor, and formed an alliance with Ahab.

verses.kjv: And after certain years he went down to Ahab to Samaria. And Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance, and for the people that he had with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.decoded: After some years, he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered many sheep and oxen for him and for the people who were with him, and convinced him to go with him to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.kjv: And Ahab king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Wilt thou go with me to Ramoth-gilead? And he answered him, I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war.
verses.decoded: And Ahab, king of Israel, said to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, 'Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?' And he answered him, 'I am like you, and my people are like your people; and we will be with you in the war.'

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Inquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord to day.
verses.decoded: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, Please ask for the word of the LORD today.

verses.kjv: Therefore the king of Israel gathered together of prophets four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for God will deliver it into the king’s hand.
verses.decoded: So the king of Israel gathered four hundred prophets and asked them, "Should we go to Ramoth-gilead to fight, or should I hold back?" They said, "Go ahead; God will give it into the king’s hand."

verses.kjv: But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord besides, that we might inquire of him?
verses.decoded: But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not another prophet of the LORD here, so that we can ask him?

verses.kjv: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, by whom we may inquire of the Lord: but I hate him; for he never prophesied good unto me, but always evil: the same is Micaiah the son of Imla. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.
verses.decoded: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can ask the LORD, but I dislike him because he never prophesies good things for me, only bad things. That man is Micaiah, the son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "Please do not say that, my king."

verses.kjv: And the king of Israel called for one of his officers, and said, Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla.
verses.decoded: The king of Israel called one of his officers and said, 'Quickly bring Micaiah, the son of Imla.'

verses.kjv: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat either of them on his throne, clothed in their robes, and they sat in a void place at the entering in of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.
verses.decoded: The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, each sat on his throne, wearing their robes, and they sat in an open area at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.

verses.kjv: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah had made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith the Lord, With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed.
verses.decoded: And Zedekiah, the son of Chenaanah, made iron horns for him and said, The LORD says, With these you will push Syria until they are completely destroyed.

verses.kjv: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and prosper: for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king.
verses.decoded: And all the prophets predicted the same thing, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, because the LORD will give it into the king's hand.

verses.kjv: And the messenger that went to call Micaiah spake to him, saying, Behold, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one assent; let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like one of theirs, and speak thou good.
verses.decoded: And the messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, the words of the prophets all agree in declaring good things to the king; so please let your word be like theirs and speak good things."

verses.kjv: And Micaiah said, As the Lord liveth, even what my God saith, that will I speak.
verses.decoded: And Micaiah said, As the LORD lives, I will speak exactly what my God says.

verses.kjv: And when he was come to the king, the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And he said, Go ye up, and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand.
verses.decoded: When he came to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to fight, or should I hold back?" He said, "Go up and succeed, and they will be given into your hand."

verses.kjv: And the king said to him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou say nothing but the truth to me in the name of the Lord?
verses.decoded: And the king said to him, How many times must I urge you to tell me only the truth in the name of the LORD?

verses.kjv: Then he said, I did see all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd: and the Lord said, These have no master; let them return therefore every man to his house in peace.
verses.decoded: Then he said, I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd; and the LORD said, They have no leader; so let each of them return to his own home in peace.

verses.kjv: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee that he would not prophesy good unto me, but evil?
verses.decoded: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good things for me, but evil?

verses.kjv: Again he said, Therefore hear the word of the Lord; I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left.
verses.decoded: He said again, So listen to the message from the LORD; I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the angels standing on his right and on his left.

verses.kjv: And the Lord said, Who shall entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one spake saying after this manner, and another saying after that manner.
verses.decoded: The LORD said, Who will persuade Ahab, king of Israel, to go up and be defeated at Ramoth-gilead? One spirit said one thing, and another spirit said something else.

verses.kjv: Then there came out a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will entice him. And the Lord said unto him, Wherewith?
verses.decoded: Then a spirit came out and stood before the LORD and said, I will entice him. And the LORD said to him, How will you do that?

verses.kjv: And he said, I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the Lord said, Thou shalt entice him, and thou shalt also prevail: go out, and do even so.
verses.decoded: And he said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets. And the LORD said, You will entice him, and you will also succeed: go out and do just that.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil against thee.
verses.decoded: So now, look, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these your prophets, and the LORD has spoken evil against you.

verses.kjv: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near, and smote Micaiah upon the cheek, and said, Which way went the Spirit of the Lord from me to speak unto thee?
verses.decoded: Then Zedekiah, the son of Chenaanah, came near and slapped Micaiah on the cheek and said, 'Which way did the Spirit of the LORD leave me to speak to you?'

verses.kjv: And Micaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see on that day when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.
verses.decoded: And Micaiah said, Look, you will see on that day when you go into a private room to hide yourself.

verses.kjv: Then the king of Israel said, Take ye Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;
verses.decoded: Then the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah and bring him back to Amon, the governor of the city, and to Joash, the king’s son;

verses.kjv: And say, Thus saith the king, Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.
verses.decoded: And say, This is what the king says: Put this man in prison, and give him bread of suffering and water of suffering until I come back safely.

verses.kjv: And Micaiah said, If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not the Lord spoken by me. And he said, Hearken, all ye people.
verses.decoded: And Micaiah said, If you definitely return safely, then the LORD has not spoken through me. And he said, Listen, all of you people.

verses.kjv: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.decoded: The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, went up to Ramoth-gilead.

verses.kjv: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes. So the king of Israel disguised himself; and they went to the battle.
verses.decoded: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went to battle.

verses.kjv: Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots that were with him, saying, Fight ye not with small or great, save only with the king of Israel.
verses.decoded: Now the king of Syria had commanded the commanders of the chariots who were with him, saying, Do not fight with anyone, whether they are of low or high rank, except only with the king of Israel.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, It is the king of Israel. Therefore they compassed about him to fight: but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord helped him; and God moved them to depart from him.
verses.decoded: When the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, 'This is the king of Israel.' So they surrounded him to fight, but Jehoshaphat shouted, and the LORD helped him; God caused them to turn away from him.

verses.kjv: For it came to pass, that, when the captains of the chariots perceived that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back again from pursuing him.
verses.decoded: It happened that when the commanders of the chariots realized it was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him and turned back.

verses.kjv: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: therefore he said to his chariot man, Turn thine hand, that thou mayest carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
verses.decoded: And a certain man shot an arrow randomly and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So he said to his chariot driver, "Turn your hand so you can take me out of the battle, because I am wounded."

verses.kjv: And the battle increased that day: howbeit the king of Israel stayed himself up in his chariot against the Syrians until the even: and about the time of the sun going down he died.
verses.decoded: The battle grew more intense that day; however, the king of Israel remained standing in his chariot against the Syrians until evening, and around sunset he died.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.
verses.decoded: Jehu, the son of Hanani the prophet, went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? That is why the LORD's anger is against you."

verses.kjv: Nevertheless there are good things found in thee, in that thou hast taken away the groves out of the land, and hast prepared thine heart to seek God.
verses.decoded: However, there are good things found in you, because you have removed the groves from the land and have set your heart to seek God.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat dwelt at Jerusalem: and he went out again through the people from Beer-sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.decoded: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out among the people from Beer-sheba to Mount Ephraim, bringing them back to the LORD God of their ancestors.

verses.kjv: And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city,
verses.decoded: He appointed judges throughout the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,

verses.kjv: And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.
verses.decoded: And said to the judges, Be careful about what you do: because you are not judging for people, but for the LORD, who is with you when you judge.

verses.kjv: Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.
verses.decoded: Therefore, now let the fear of the LORD be on you; pay attention and do it, because there is no wrongdoing with the LORD our God, no favoritism, and no accepting of bribes.

verses.kjv: Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Israel, for the judgment of the Lord, and for controversies, when they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: Also, in Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, some of the priests, and some of the leaders of the families of Israel to serve as judges for the Lord and to settle disputes when they returned to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And he charged them, saying, Thus shall ye do in the fear of the Lord, faithfully, and with a perfect heart.
verses.decoded: And he instructed them, saying, This is how you should act with reverence for the LORD, faithfully, and with a sincere heart.

verses.kjv: And what cause soever shall come to you of your brethren that dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgments, ye shall even warn them that they trespass not against the Lord, and so wrath come upon you, and upon your brethren: this do, and ye shall not trespass.
verses.decoded: And whatever dispute comes to you from your fellow Israelites living in their towns, whether it is about murder, laws, commands, statutes, or judgments, you must warn them not to sin against the LORD, so that his anger will not come upon you or your fellow Israelites. Do this, and you will not sin.

verses.kjv: And, behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the Lord; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, for all the king’s matters: also the Levites shall be officers before you. Deal courageously, and the Lord shall be with the good.
verses.decoded: Look, Amariah the chief priest is in charge of all matters concerning the LORD for you; and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, is in charge of all the king’s matters; also, the Levites will serve as officers before you. Act bravely, and the LORD will be with those who do what is right.

verses.kjv: It came to pass after this also, that the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them other beside the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat to battle.
verses.decoded: After this, the people of Moab and the people of Ammon, along with others from beyond the Ammonites, came to fight against Jehoshaphat.

verses.kjv: Then there came some that told Jehoshaphat, saying, There cometh a great multitude against thee from beyond the sea on this side Syria; and, behold, they be in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi.
verses.decoded: Then some people came and told Jehoshaphat, saying, A great crowd is coming against you from across the sea on this side of Syria; and look, they are Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat feared, and set himself to seek the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
verses.decoded: Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he decided to seek the LORD and announced a fast throughout all Judah.

verses.kjv: And Judah gathered themselves together, to ask help of the Lord: even out of all the cities of Judah they came to seek the Lord.
verses.decoded: And the people of Judah gathered together to ask the Lord for help; from all the cities of Judah they came to seek the Lord.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,
verses.decoded: And Jehoshaphat stood among the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, in front of the new courtyard,

verses.kjv: And said, O Lord God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee?
verses.decoded: And said, O LORD God of our ancestors, are you not God in heaven? Do you not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? Is there not power and strength in your hand, so that no one can resist you?

verses.kjv: Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?
verses.decoded: Are you not our God, who drove out the people living in this land before your people Israel, and gave it to the descendants of Abraham your friend forever?

verses.kjv: And they dwelt therein, and have built thee a sanctuary therein for thy name, saying,
verses.decoded: And they lived there, and have built you a sanctuary there for your name, saying,

verses.kjv: If, when evil cometh upon us, as the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we stand before this house, and in thy presence, (for thy name is in this house,) and cry unto thee in our affliction, then thou wilt hear and help.
verses.decoded: If, when trouble comes to us, like war, punishment, disease, or hunger, we stand in front of this temple, and in your presence, (because your name is in this temple,) and call out to you in our trouble, then you will listen and help.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not;
verses.decoded: And now, look, the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, whom you did not allow Israel to attack when they came out of Egypt, but you turned away from them and did not destroy them;

verses.kjv: Behold, I say, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit.
verses.decoded: Look, I say, how they repay us by coming to drive us out of your land, which you gave us to inherit.

verses.kjv: O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.
verses.decoded: O our God, will you not judge them? For we have no power against this large group coming against us; we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.

verses.kjv: And all Judah stood before the Lord, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
verses.decoded: All the people of Judah stood in front of the LORD, along with their young children, their wives, and their children.

verses.kjv: Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, came the Spirit of the Lord in the midst of the congregation;
verses.decoded: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel, the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite from the family of Asaph, while he was among the people;

verses.kjv: And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the Lord unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
verses.decoded: And he said, Listen all of Judah, and all people living in Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat, This is what the LORD says to you: Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this large crowd; the battle is not yours, but God's.

verses.kjv: To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel.
verses.decoded: Tomorrow go down against them: look, they are coming up by the cliff of Ziz; and you will find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

verses.kjv: Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the Lord with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the Lord will be with you.
verses.decoded: You will not need to fight in this battle: prepare yourselves, stand still, and watch the LORD's salvation with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: do not fear or be discouraged; tomorrow go out against them, because the LORD will be with you.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the Lord, worshipping the Lord.
verses.decoded: And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the people living in Jerusalem fell down before the LORD, worshiping the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the Levites, of the children of the Kohathites, and of the children of the Korhites, stood up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high.
verses.decoded: The Levites, from the families of the Kohathites and the Korhites, stood up to loudly praise the LORD God of Israel.

verses.kjv: And they rose early in the morning, and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa: and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Hear me, O Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem; Believe in the Lord your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper.
verses.decoded: They got up early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Listen to me, people of Judah and all who live in Jerusalem: Trust in the LORD your God, and you will be secure; trust in his prophets, and you will succeed.

verses.kjv: And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the Lord, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the Lord; for his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.decoded: After he had talked with the people, he assigned singers to the LORD, who would praise the beauty of holiness as they went ahead of the army, saying, 'Praise the LORD, for his mercy lasts forever.'

verses.kjv: And when they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.
verses.decoded: When they started to sing and praise, the LORD set up ambushes against the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.

verses.kjv: For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy them: and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.
verses.decoded: The people of Ammon and Moab rose up against the people living on Mount Seir to completely kill and destroy them. After they finished destroying the people of Seir, they then helped to destroy each other.

verses.kjv: And when Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked unto the multitude, and, behold, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.
verses.decoded: When Judah approached the watchtower in the wilderness, they looked at the crowd and saw that they were dead bodies lying on the ground, and no one had escaped.

verses.kjv: And when Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoil of them, they found among them in abundance both riches with the dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away: and they were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much.
verses.decoded: When Jehoshaphat and his people went to collect the plunder from them, they found a large amount of riches among the dead bodies, including precious jewels, which they took for themselves. There was more than they could carry, and it took them three days to gather all the spoil because there was so much.

verses.kjv: And on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Berachah; for there they blessed the Lord: therefore the name of the same place was called, The valley of Berachah, unto this day.
verses.decoded: On the fourth day, they gathered together in the valley of Berachah because there they praised the LORD. That is why the place was named the valley of Berachah, up to this day.

verses.kjv: Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for the Lord had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
verses.decoded: Then every man from Judah and Jerusalem returned, with Jehoshaphat leading them, to go back to Jerusalem with joy because the LORD had caused them to celebrate their victory over their enemies.

verses.kjv: And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries and harps and trumpets unto the house of the Lord.
verses.decoded: And they came to Jerusalem with stringed instruments, harps, and trumpets to the house of the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of those countries, when they had heard that the Lord fought against the enemies of Israel.
verses.decoded: All the kingdoms in those regions were afraid of God when they heard that the LORD had fought against Israel's enemies.

verses.kjv: So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his God gave him rest round about.
verses.decoded: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was peaceful because his God gave him rest all around.

verses.kjv: And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah: he was thirty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
verses.decoded: Jehoshaphat ruled over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to rule, and he ruled for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

verses.kjv: And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and departed not from it, doing that which was right in the sight of the Lord.
verses.decoded: He followed the example of Asa his father and did not turn away from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.kjv: Howbeit the high places were not taken away: for as yet the people had not prepared their hearts unto the God of their fathers.
verses.decoded: However, the high places were not removed because the people had not yet made their hearts ready to worship the God of their ancestors.

verses.kjv: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Jehu the son of Hanani, who is mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.
verses.decoded: The rest of the actions of Jehoshaphat, from beginning to end, are written in the book of Jehu, the son of Hanani, who is mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.

verses.kjv: And after this did Jehoshaphat king of Judah join himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly:
verses.decoded: After this, Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, allied himself with Ahaziah, king of Israel, who acted very wickedly.

verses.kjv: And he joined himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish: and they made the ships in Ezion-geber.
verses.decoded: He partnered with him to build ships to sail to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-gaber.

verses.kjv: Then Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the Lord hath broken thy works. And the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.
verses.decoded: Then Eliezer, the son of Dodavah from Mareshah, spoke a prophecy against Jehoshaphat, saying, Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has ruined your plans. And the ships were destroyed so that they could not sail to Tarshish.

verses.kjv: Now Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.
verses.decoded: Now Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. Then his son Jehoram became king in his place.

verses.kjv: And he had brethren the sons of Jehoshaphat, Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah: all these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
verses.decoded: He had brothers: the sons of Jehoshaphat were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All of these were the sons of Jehoshaphat, king of Israel.

verses.kjv: And their father gave them great gifts of silver, and of gold, and of precious things, with fenced cities in Judah: but the kingdom gave he to Jehoram; because he was the firstborn.
verses.decoded: Their father gave them large gifts of silver, gold, and valuable items, along with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the oldest son.

verses.kjv: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Israel.
verses.decoded: When Jehoram became king after his father, he made himself strong and killed all his brothers with the sword, as well as several of the leaders of Israel.

verses.kjv: Jehoram was thirty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to rule, and he ruled for eight years in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.decoded: He followed the example of the kings of Israel, just like the family of Ahab did, because he married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.kjv: Howbeit the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.
verses.decoded: However, the LORD did not destroy the family of David because of the agreement he had made with David, and because he promised to give a lasting light to him and his descendants forever.

verses.kjv: In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king.
verses.decoded: During his reign, the Edomites rebelled against the control of Judah and appointed their own king.

verses.kjv: Then Jehoram went forth with his princes, and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him in, and the captains of the chariots.
verses.decoded: Then Jehoram went out with his officials and all his chariots. He got up during the night and attacked the Edomites who had surrounded him, and he defeated the commanders of the chariots.

verses.kjv: So the Edomites revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. The same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.
verses.decoded: So the Edomites rebelled against the control of Judah up to this day. At the same time, Libnah also rebelled against his control because he had abandoned the LORD God of his ancestors.

verses.kjv: Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and compelled Judah thereto.
verses.decoded: In addition, he built worship sites on the hills of Judah, led the people living in Jerusalem to commit sexual immorality, and forced the people of Judah to do the same.

verses.kjv: And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, Thus saith the Lord God of David thy father, Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.decoded: A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, This is what the LORD God of David your father says: Because you have not followed the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, nor the ways of Asa king of Judah,

verses.kjv: But hast walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and hast made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father’s house, which were better than thyself:
verses.decoded: But you have followed the ways of the kings of Israel, and you have caused Judah and the people of Jerusalem to be unfaithful, like the unfaithfulness of the family of Ahab, and you have also killed your brothers from your father’s family, who were better than you.

verses.kjv: Behold, with a great plague will the Lord smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods:
verses.decoded: Look, the LORD will strike your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions with a great plague.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.
verses.decoded: And you will have a severe illness caused by disease in your intestines, until your intestines come out because of the sickness day after day.

verses.kjv: Moreover the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians:
verses.decoded: Furthermore, the LORD caused the Philistines and the Arabians, who lived near the Ethiopians, to rise up against Jehoram.

verses.kjv: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
verses.decoded: They came into Judah, broke into it, and took away all the wealth found in the king’s house, along with his sons and his wives; so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

verses.kjv: And after all this the Lord smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease.
verses.decoded: After all this, the LORD struck him in his internal organs with a disease that could not be cured.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that in process of time, after the end of two years, his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers.
verses.decoded: And it happened that after two years, his intestines came out because of his illness, so he died from severe diseases. And his people did not make a funeral fire for him like the funeral fires for his ancestors.

verses.kjv: Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years, and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.
verses.decoded: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years, and he died without being mourned. However, they buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

verses.kjv: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
verses.decoded: The people living in Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king instead of him because the group of men who came with the Arabians to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, became king.

verses.kjv: Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
verses.decoded: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was also Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.

verses.kjv: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counseller to do wickedly.
verses.decoded: He also followed the practices of the family of Ahab, because his mother advised him to do evil.

verses.kjv: Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellers after the death of his father to his destruction.
verses.decoded: Therefore, he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just like the family of Ahab, because they were his advisors after his father's death, leading him to his ruin.

verses.kjv: He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead: and the Syrians smote Joram.
verses.decoded: He also followed their advice and went with Jehoram, the son of Ahab, king of Israel, to fight against Hazael, king of Syria, at Ramoth-gilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram.

verses.kjv: And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick.
verses.decoded: He went back to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds he received at Ramah when he fought against Hazael, the king of Syria. Azariah, the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to visit Jehoram, the son of Ahab, at Jezreel because he was ill.

verses.kjv: And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
verses.decoded: And Ahaziah's destruction was caused by God when he went to Joram: because when he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to fight against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had chosen to destroy the family of Ahab.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them.
verses.decoded: It happened that when Jehu was carrying out judgment against the house of Ahab, he found the leaders of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's relatives who served Ahaziah, and he killed them.

verses.kjv: And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom.
verses.decoded: He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him because he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu, and after they killed him, they buried him. They said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." Therefore, the family of Ahaziah could not maintain control over the kingdom.

verses.kjv: But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah.
verses.decoded: But when Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she got up and killed all the royal descendants of the house of Judah.

verses.kjv: But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not.
